Arrange pieces of text into lines

Source: R/layout_lines.R
layout_lines.Rd

Give the line of each piece of a text, from their widths, for a maximum width. This is the part shared by gen_grob() and the packages that draw rich text with 'grid'.

A piece that makes the line too wide goes to the next line, except if it is the first of its line. Spaces are dropped when they do not fit and at the start of a line that follows an automatic line break; they are kept after a line break of the text, as they were written. A line break ends its line, and gives a line of its own if that line is empty.

A word wider than a line is first moved to a new line, then split between its characters: give its characters as pieces and set break_before to TRUE on the first one.

Usage

layout_lines(
  width,
  newline,
  space,
  max_width,
  first_line = 0,
  hanging = 0,
  break_before = FALSE
)

Arguments

width

widths of the pieces.

newline, space

logical vectors, TRUE for the line breaks and the spaces.

max_width

maximum width of a line, Inf for no automatic line break.

first_line, hanging

width removed from the first line, and from the other lines.

break_before

logical, TRUE for the pieces that start a new line unless the current line is empty. It is recycled to the length of width.

Value

An integer vector, the line of each piece, 0 for the dropped pieces.

Examples

layout_lines(
  width = c(2, 1, 2, 1, 3),
  newline = rep(FALSE, 5),
  space = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE),
  max_width = 5
)
#> [1] 1 1 1 0 2
